title: Read the verse next door
note: Written fresh on 2026-11-26 at James's word: "I want you to have liberty to write the scripts." Not recorded, and James has not read it yet. Every fact is listed with where to check it in facts.md beside this file. Scripture is the Berean Standard Bible, copied word for word from client/public/bible/text/; an exclamation mark appears only where the verse has one. Field names and `gap` follow James's description of the Gather scripts; match them to film/beliefs/script.json on the Mac.

lines: You've seen this one. On gym walls. On locker room doors.
I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.

scripture.text: I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.

lines: It sounds like a promise that you'll win.
So here's the first rule of reading the Bible. Read the verse next door.
Paul wrote this letter as a prisoner, in chains.
And one sentence earlier, he tells you what all things means.
Being filled and being hungry. Having plenty and having need.

scripture.text: to being filled and being hungry, to having plenty and having need

lines: All things isn't winning. It's the full days and the hungry days. It's being all right when you lose.
That's a better promise than the one on the wall. It doesn't say you'll get what you want.
It says Christ will be enough when you don't.
So before you quote a verse, read the ones around it.
